s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with radiation to the jaw and diaphoresis
salient_findings: Chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression on ECG
key_facts: Subjective fevers, rhinorrhea, dry cough, and sinus congestion 4 days prior to presentation
3 hours of substernal pressure that resolved spontaneously the day prior to presentation
Constant chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein
Initial serum troponin I level of 6.18 ng/mL
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with radiation to the jaw and diaphoresis
salient_findings: Chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression on ECG
key_facts: Subjective fevers, rhinorrhea, dry cough, and sinus congestion 4 days prior to presentation
3 hours of substernal pressure that resolved spontaneously the day prior to presentation
Constant chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein
Initial serum troponin I level of 6.18 ng/mL
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography

differentials: Acute coronary syndrome due to coronary artery thrombosis
per_call: Acute coronary syndrome due to coronary artery thrombosis

shortlist.label: Myopericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin, ST-segment elevations, and PR-segment depression suggest myocardial involvement, while normal coronary arteries and echocardiogram results point towards an inflammatory process

shortlist.label: Pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pain radiating to the jaw, diaphoresis, and vomiting, along with ST-segment elevations and PR-segment depression, are consistent with pericarditis

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin, normal coronary arteries, and normal echocardiogram results, combined with recent symptoms of a viral illness, suggest a possible inflammatory myocardial process

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin and chest pressure radiating to the jaw are concerning for myocardial infarction, although normal coronary arteries on angiography make this less likely

shortlist.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Transient chest pressure, diaphoresis, and vomiting, along with elevated troponin and normal coronary arteries, could be consistent with stress-induced cardiomyopathy

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with chest pressure, elevated troponin, and ST-segment elevations on ECG, along with elevated inflammatory markers and normal coronary arteries, suggests an inflammatory process affecting both the myocardium and pericardium.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: Normal coronary arteries on angiography make this diagnosis unlikely

rejected.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic wall motion abnormalities on echocardiogram

rejected.label: Pericarditis
rejected.why: Elevated troponin and PR-segment depression in multiple leads suggest myocardial involvement

rejected.label: Myocarditis
rejected.why: ECG findings and elevated inflammatory markers are more consistent with myopericarditis, which involves both myocardial and pericardial inflammation
